agent: agreements wave, brief A (an offer's way through the game)
question: Who answers a diplomatic offer, when, and how the player takes part: 0x89E010 read whole, the pending list's other readers, the offer shown to the player and his answer, and the reader of next_offer_allowed.

addresses.name: CAIForeignMinister::AnswerPendingOffers
addresses.comment:
**How an AI country answers the offers made to it.** 0x89E010 to the `ret 4` at 0x89E273, the minister on the stack, ECX unused. Two callers: ProcessAI at 0x8896F7, **every hour, for every CEU3AI whose foreign minister (+0x60) exists, with no test of the agent's enable byte or of the hour**, and CAIForeignMinister::DoWork at 0x89D67D, once a day at the minister's hour, just before ForeignMinister_Tick. So in practice an offer is answered in the first AI pass after it arrives.

Walks the minister's country's pending list (CCountry +0xF24) front to back - arrival order - and for each action:

    if (!action->slot18() || action->type != PROPOSE) continue;      // left unanswered, and dropped below
    score = action->GetAIAcceptance();                                 // slot 17, the mod's Lua
    if (score <= 30) -> DECLINE                                        // 0x89E0A5, `jle 0x1E` - no roll is drawn
    roll = MT19937Next(&gamestate->+0x124) % 100                       // the game state's generator, 0x89E132
    if (roll >= score) -> DECLINE                                      // 0x89E13F, accept only when roll < score
    if (action->GetToken() != trade_action 0x6DA) -> ACCEPT
    else if (no trade accepted yet this call) -> ACCEPT, and remember one was
    else keep it, still PROPOSE, on a local list

An answer writes `type` (2 ACCEPT at 0x89E1E7/0x89E16B, 1 DECLINE at 0x89E1F0) **on the pending action itself**, then MakeCommand (slot 6) clones it and the command is posted through country->+0xF1C slot 18 -> +0x38 slot 6. At the end CCountry::RetainPendingDiplomaticActions (0xE6410) deletes every action on the list but the kept trades, which stay PROPOSE and are rolled again on the next call. The draw comes from the shared game-state generator on a TBB worker thread (ProcessAI's thread), so which country draws first is not fixed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md.
addresses.evidence: Read whole off the disassembly (disasm.py 0x89E010 0x270) and cross-read with Ghidra's decompilation; the two callers from findRefs --callers (exactly two, 0x8896F7 and 0x89D67D); ProcessAI 0x8896EC-0x8896F7 read: `mov eax,[ecx+0x60]; test; je; push eax; call` with nothing testing +0x3C on that path; MT19937Next's result is non-negative per its record, so the remainder is 0..99. Shown wrong by a path into the PROPOSE branch that does not test slot 18, or a second caller.

addresses.name: CCountry::RetainPendingDiplomaticActions
addresses.comment: Replaces a country's pending list (+0xF24) by the actions on `keep`. 0x4E6410 to the `ret 4` at 0x4E64A1, the country in EAX, the list on the stack. With `keep` empty it is CCountry::ClearPendingDiplomaticActions (rva 0xE63A0, with EDI = the country). Otherwise it deletes (slot 0, 1) every pending action whose pointer is not on `keep`, frees every node, zeroes head, tail and count, and appends `keep`'s actions back through CList::AppendAllNodes (rva 0x49C070, source EAX, destination ESI = &country->+0xF24). The kept actions are the same objects, not copies. Three callers: CAIForeignMinister::AnswerPendingOffers (0x89E242), CEU3Idler::Update (0x644ADC) and CCountry::RunHourlyAITrade (0x4DC652) - in each the caller builds `keep` as the trade offers it wants to carry over.
addresses.evidence: Read whole (disasm.py 0x4E6410 0xA0): the count test at 0x4E641A, the membership walk 0x4E6437-0x4E6460, the node frees 0x4E6470, the three zeroing stores and the call to 0x89C070 at 0x4E6499 with ESI = country+0xF24. Shown wrong by a caller that passes the country anywhere but EAX.

addresses.name: CEU3Idler::Update
addresses.revises: comment only: the tail this entry said was not read (0x644937-0x644B02) is read - it is where the player is shown the offers made to him. Name, signature and the dialog-list reading are kept.
addresses.comment:
Slot 1 of CEU3Idler. Read only as far as the dialog list: it calls slot 1 of every updateable at +0xA0 and collects those answering false; each collected one is unlinked from the list (or, while +0xAC is set, only marked at node +0xC) and deleted through its slot 0. The stack argument is unread per CInGameIdler::Update's record.

**The tail (0x644937-0x644B02) shows the player the offers made to him, every frame.** It finds the local player record (the inlined CGameState::GetLocalPlayer) and does nothing when that record's first delegation flag is 1 (`mov ecx,[rec+0x38]; cmp dword [ecx],1` at 0x644937 - foreign policy left to the AI, whose minister then answers through CAIForeignMinister::AnswerPendingOffers). Otherwise it takes the player's country from this->slot 23 (GetPlayer) and walks its pending list (+0xF24): a `trade_action` (token 0x6DA) is kept on a local list **when the record's byte +0x34 is set** - that byte is `automate_trade`, written by CGameState::LoadKey's automate_trade arm (0x68066F-0x680698, ParseBool into GetLocalPlayer()+0x34) - and every other action gets its slot 19 (AskPlayer) with `this`, which for a PROPOSE of a kind the player answers makes a CAsk* dialog and hands it to CInGameIdler::AddDiplomaticOffer. Then CCountry::RetainPendingDiplomaticActions (0xE6410) empties the list but the kept trades, which CCountry::RunHourlyAITrade answers. So each offer is shown once: by the next frame it is off the list. The tail is read in full; the entry stays `inferred` because the dialog-list half before it is still the earlier partial reading. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfire.md.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x644750-0x644B33 and the decompilation; GetLocalPlayer()+0x34 = automate_trade from the CGameState::LoadKey token comparison `cmp eax, 0x737` at 0x680211 (`je 0x68066F`) and the store at 0x680698. Shown wrong by the 0x737 case not being automate_trade (saveTokens) or by a second writer of +0x34 that disagrees.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::AddDiplomaticOffer
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CInGameIdler::AddDiplomaticOffer(CInGameIdler* this, CDiplomacyDialog* dialog, int kind, CCountryTag* from)
addresses.comment: **Virtual slot 24 of CInGameIdler, the one place an offer to the player is put on screen.** `ret 0xC`. When the local player record's byte +0x28 (the popup gate FireEvent also reads) is clear the dialog is deleted through its slot 0 and the offer is gone - no reply is ever sent. Otherwise DiploIconBar_Add(this->+0x1D38, dialog, kind, from): an icon with the proposer's flag in the in-game screen's diplomatic message bar, which opens the dialog when clicked. The callers are the action classes' slot 19 (AskPlayer), each passing its own `kind`: 1 peace, 2 alliance, 3 trade, 4 military access asked, 5 military access offered, 6 call to arms, 7 non-aggression pact, 8 faction, 9 expeditionary force, 10 licence, 11 debt, 12 lend-lease asked, 13 lend-lease offered.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x674EF0-0x674FD6: GetLocalPlayer at 0x674F85, `cmp byte [eax+0x28], bl` at 0x674F8A, the delete arm at 0x674FB8, `mov edi,[edi+0x1D38]` and the call to 0x61A1D0 at 0x674FA1. vtable.py --holding: one table, CInGameIdler slot 24. The kinds are the immediates pushed before `call [edx+0x60]` in the thirteen slot-19 bodies. Shown wrong by another holder of the body.

addresses.name: CDiploIcon::Update
addresses.comment: **The time limit on an offer the player has not opened.** `ret 8`, the icon in EDI, a double (the screen's clock, used only to blink) on the stack. Returns false - remove me - when the icon was clicked (+0x7C). Otherwise, with now = g_CCurrentGameState->tick: while now <= +0x20 (seven days after the icon appeared) it stays; between +0x1C and +0x20 (days five to seven) a laid-out icon (+0x7D) blinks, its button's alpha toggled on (int)(time x k) % 5. **Once now > +0x20 it calls the dialog's slot 6 (CDiplomacyDialog::Decline) and returns false**: an offer left unanswered for seven days is declined for the player, with the reply posted like a pressed Decline.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x619BF0-0x619D77: `cmp byte [edi+0x7c]` at 0x619C0F, the three compares at 0x619C9A/0x619CA3/0x619D57, `call [edx+0x18]` on [edi+4] at 0x619D64. One caller, DiploIconBar_Update. Shown wrong by slot 6 of a CAsk* table being anything but CDiplomacyDialog::Decline (vtable.py shows all twelve inherit 0x60FB20).

addresses.name: CDiploIcon::OnClick
addresses.comment: The press of an offer's icon, bound by CDiploIcon::CDiploIcon to `diplomessageicon_button`. Shows the dialog's window (dialog slots 12 and 9), hands the dialog to CEU3Idler::AddDialog on the in-game screen - where CEU3Dialog::Update runs it every frame - clears the icon's dialog pointer and sets +0x7C so the bar drops the icon. From here the dialog's own slot 7 is its only time limit.

Positions the bar, runs CDiploIcon::Update on each icon, and deletes every icon that answers false - its window through slot 20 and its dialog through slot 0, so an icon dropped this way takes its dialog (and the dialog's copy of the action) with it - then lays the bar out again.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyDialog::Accept
addresses.comment: **What the player's Accept does.** Slot 5, bound to `AgreeButton` by CEU3Dialog's constructor (0x63D4B0, through the shared `jmp [eax+0x14]` thunk at 0x6FB9A0). Sets the dialog's action (+0x6C) `type = 2` (ACCEPT), MakeCommand (slot 6) and posts the command through the host (+0x68) slot 18 -> +0x38 slot 6, then marks the dialog closed (+0x64 = 1). No other test: the reply is checked only where every peer checks it, in CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute's IsValid. Inherited by all twelve CAsk* dialogs.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x60FAE0-0x60FB15; vtable.py shows 0x60FAE0 at slot 5 of CDiplomacyDialog and all twelve CAsk* classes and nowhere else; the binding of AgreeButton to slot 5 and DeclineButton to slot 6 is read off 0x63D4ED/0x63D518 and the thunks 0x6FB9A0 (`jmp [eax+0x14]`) and 0x998430 (`jmp [eax+0x18]`).

addresses.name: CDiplomacyDialog::Decline
addresses.comment: **What the player's Decline does - and what every time limit on an offer to him does.** Slot 6, bound to `DeclineButton`. The same as CDiplomacyDialog::Accept with `type = 1` (DECLINE). Also called by CDiploIcon::Update when an unopened offer is seven days old, and by the dialogs' slot 7 when an open offer has expired or stopped being possible - so a lapsed offer is always answered with a DECLINE the proposer hears about.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x60FB20-0x60FB55; the callers through slot 6 read at 0x619D64, 0x60FC1A, 0x610725 and the five CAsk* slot 7 overrides.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyDialog::IsStillOpen
addresses.comment: Slot 7, asked every frame by CEU3Dialog::Update (slot 1, 0x63D830) for an open dialog; false closes it. Base rule, kept by CAskOfferMilitaryAccess, CAskFaction, CAskPeace, CAskDebt, CAskLendLease and CAskBuyLicence: **expires = AddMonths(action->date, 2)**; if expires < now, Decline (slot 6) and false; if the action's IsValid (slot 13) is false, Decline and false; otherwise open while `type == 0`. So an opened offer lapses two months after it was made, counted from the action's own `date` - not from when the player saw it.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x60FB60-0x60FC58: AddMonths (rva 0xB8C90) with EAX = &date and 2 pushed at 0x60FB89, `cmp ecx,[esi+0xbdc]; jge` at 0x60FC0B, `call [edx+0x34]` (slot 13) at 0x60FC37, `sete al` on +0x18. vtable.py --holding: seven tables, CDiplomacyDialog and the six CAsk* classes that inherit it.

addresses.name: RunCountryDailyPass_ExpirePendingActions
addresses.no_signature: an instruction inside RunCountryDailyPass, not a function
addresses.comment: `xor edi, edi` - the start of the block in RunCountryDailyPass (0x4DB042-0x4DB179) that **deletes, unanswered, every pending action (CCountry +0xF24) whose last_command_date + 0x60 (96 hours, four days) is before today's tick**. It runs for a country with a CEU3AI that nobody plays, and for the local player's own country only while his first delegation flag is 1 (foreign policy left to the AI) - so never for an undelegated player. In practice what it catches are the trade offers AnswerPendingOffers keeps back (only one trade is accepted per pass); they are dropped four days after they arrived. Removal honours the list's no_unlink byte (+0xF30), marking the node instead of unlinking it while that is set.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x4DAFBC-0x4DB179: the gates (+0x1D8, played_countries_array, GetLocalPlayer()+0x38[0] == 1), `mov eax,[eax+0x20]; add eax,0x60; cmp [ebp-0x28],eax; jle` at 0x4DB064-0x4DB06D, [ebp-0x28] = tick from 0x4DA5CD-0x4DA5D4, delete through slot 0 at 0x4DB0C6, the unlink and `cmp byte [ebx+0xf30],0` at 0x4DB101. functionStart answers 0x4DAE94, which is not an entry; RunCountryDailyPass's extent (0x4DA530-0x4DC239) holds it with retsBefore empty.

addresses.name: RunHourlyPass_TutorialAcceptAll
addresses.no_signature: an instruction inside RunHourlyPass, not a function
addresses.comment: `mov ecx, [edi+0xBC0]` - the loop RunHourlyPass runs **instead of re-arming the AI pass** when tutorial_active (+0xD9D) is set (`jne 0x682B37` at 0x682B1B). For every country nobody plays it accepts each pending PROPOSE whose slot 18 is true (type = 2 at 0x682BB3, MakeCommand, posted through +0xF1C) and then clears the country's pending list (0x682BE5). **It is the tutorial's AI, not the ordinary game's**: in an ordinary game the clear of ai_pass_done at 0x682B1D runs instead and offers are answered by CAIForeignMinister::AnswerPendingOffers. FINDINGS-diploaction.md section 5 described this loop as the AI's answer; that is corrected in FINDINGS-agreements.md.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from RunHourlyPass's entry 0x682630 to 0x682C20: `cmp byte [esi+0xd9d],0; jne 0x682b37` at 0x682B14, the loop 0x682B37-0x682C07. tutorial_active's writers are the two CTutorialScreen handlers (its record).

addresses.name: CDiplomaticAction::MakeCommand
addresses.revises: comment only: it said the hourly AI pass at 0x682BC2 is 'its one caller inside the engine'. That loop runs only in the tutorial, and slot 6 is called from at least nine places, listed. Name, signature and confidence unchanged.
addresses.comment:
Slot 6, and the base's own body in all 24 tables of the family - the step that turns an action into something postable. Lazily creates g_CCurrentGameState, stamps `this->last_command_date` (+0x20) with its tick (+0xBDC) at 0xA0E92D, asks `operator new` for 0x40 bytes (sizeof CDiplomaticActionCommand), clones itself through slot 16 (0xA0E94F) and hands the clone to CDiplomaticActionCommand's two-argument constructor (0xA0E090 at 0xA0E953), returning the command. It does not post it: every caller pushes the result onto the session's command channel (country->+0xF1C slot 18 -> session +0x38 slot 6). Bare `ret`, no stack arguments, receiver in ECX.

Its callers (virtual, so found by reading, not counted): CAIForeignMinister::AnswerPendingOffers (an AI's answers), CCountry::RunHourlyAITrade (the player's trades under automate_trade), CEU3AI::PostAction (an offer from Lua), CDiplomacyDialog::Accept and ::Decline (the player's answer), DiplomacyDialog_OnAgree (rva 0x373090, the player's own offer), CCallAllyAction::AskPlayer (a call to arms accepted unasked), and the tutorial's accept-all loop at 0x682BC2.
addresses.evidence: The callers were each read posting its result: 0x89E184/0x89E20B, 0x4DC5B8/0x4DC5E9, 0x49A750's body, 0x60FAF6/0x60FB36, 0x773141, 0xA2ACF4, 0x682BC2. Shown wrong by any of them not calling slot 6 of a CDiplomaticAction.

addresses.name: CCountry::ClearPendingDiplomaticActions
addresses.revises: comment only: it said the hourly AI pass runs it 'on every AI country ... so an offer not acted on in the hour it arrives is discarded'. That pass is the tutorial's; the ordinary game's clearing goes through CCountry::RetainPendingDiplomaticActions. Signature kept as recorded.
addresses.comment: Deletes every action in the +0xF24 list through its slot 0 with the free flag, frees every node, and zeroes +0xF24, +0xF28 and +0xF2C. Receiver in EDI, no stack arguments, bare `ret`. Callers: CCountry::RetainPendingDiplomaticActions (rva 0xE6410) when nothing is to be kept - which is how AnswerPendingOffers, CEU3Idler::Update and RunHourlyAITrade empty a list - and the tutorial's accept-all loop in RunHourlyPass at 0x682BE5.
addresses.evidence: The call at 0x4E6420 inside 0x4E6410 (EDI = EAX = the country) and the one at 0x682BE5; the tutorial gate at 0x682B14.

addresses.name: CCountry::RunHourlyAITrade
addresses.revises: comment only: adds the block in front of the Lua calls (0x4DC4A6-0x4DC66B) that answers the player's own trade offers under automate_trade. The Lua half is kept word for word.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x4DC4A6-0x4DC66B: the three gates at 0x4DC4BD/0x4DC4C9/0x4DC4D6, `mov [ebp-0x2c], 1` at 0x4DC4DF, the two LCG steps 0x4DC559-0x4DC582 (0x343FD, 0x269EC3), `idiv 0x64; cmp edx, edi; jge` at 0x4DC58C-0x4DC595, the call to 0x4E6410 at 0x4DC652. The roll sequence computed from those constants. Shown wrong by [ebp-0x2c] being written anywhere else in the function before 0x4DC559.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyStatus::SetNextOfferAllowed
addresses.revises: comment and confidence: the field now has a reader (CCountry::HasDiplomatEnroute, rva 0xE3ED0, found by brief B of the same wave and found again here by an independent scan), so the cooldown is no longer inference. The signature places its stack argument explicitly; the convention is unchanged.
addresses.comment: Stores its argument in the status's +0x50 (next_offer_allowed, the save's `last_send_diplomat`). The body is `status->+0x50 = when` on both arms of a comparison against `g_CCurrentGameState->tick + 0xA8` (0xA4A5E6, `jle`), so the comparison is dead. One caller: CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute passes `action->date + 0xA8` - the proposal's date plus 168 hours, exactly seven days - on the PROPOSE path for every kind but `callaction`, on the proposer's status toward the recipient, whatever the answer turns out to be. **The reader is CCountry::HasDiplomatEnroute (rva 0xE3ED0)**: `tick <= +0x50`, registered to Lua and used by the diplomacy screen to grey a row (ENROUTE, "We have a diplomat enroute, and he will arrive on $DATE$") and by the shipped AI scripts (ai_foreign_minister.lua, ai_trade.lua, ai_support_functions.lua) before they post. So it is a seven-day cooldown on one country's offers to another, enforced where an offer is chosen and **not** in Execute. Receiver in EDI, one stack argument, `ret 4`.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0xA4A5DB-0xA4A606 for the dead compare; the reader 0x4E3F68-0x4E3F76 (`mov ecx,[esi+0xbdc]; cmp ecx,[edi+0x50]; setle al`, EDI = this->+0xE28[other]). A scan of every [reg+0x50] (reg not ESP/EBP) in the diplomacy code ranges 0xA0D000-0xA4D000, 0x4E0000-0x4E7000, 0x770000-0x792000, 0x60F000-0x61D000 and 0x89C000-0x8A0000 returned 57 sites; its positive controls are this setter's three accesses and LoadKey's `lea esi,[ebx+0x50]` at 0xA482CB, and the one read through a status pointer is 0x4E3F6E. The GUI hits are `mov eax,[edx+0x50]` virtual calls. The Lua uses grepped in the install's script/ and tfh/script/.

structs.name: CEU3Dialog
structs.comment: The base of every in-game dialog (46 tables). Its constructor (rva 0x23D4B0) makes the window and binds `AgreeButton` to slot 5 and `DeclineButton` to slot 6; slot 1 (rva 0x23D830) is the per-frame update the idler's dialog list runs, which first asks slot 7 and drops the dialog when that answers false.
structs.evidence: RTTI export (vftable 0x015CD334, base CUpdateable); the constructor 0x63D4B0 decompiled and its two button bindings read at 0x63D4ED and 0x63D518.

structs.name: CDiplomacyDialog
structs.comment: The base of the twelve CAsk* dialogs that put an offer to the player (and of CWarGoalDialog).
structs.evidence: RTTI export (vftable 0x015CB2EC, base CEU3Dialog at offset 0); every AskPlayer body allocates 0x70 bytes for a CAsk* dialog and no CAsk* class adds a field written past +0x6C.

structs.name: CDiploIcon
structs.comment: One icon in the in-game screen's diplomatic message bar - an offer waiting for the player. Not polymorphic: +0x0 is its window, and the class is named only by its CButtonObserverGlue<CDiploIcon>. Built by CDiploIcon::CDiploIcon (rva 0x219720).
structs.evidence: new(0x80) at 0x61A1F0 immediately before the constructor call; the RTTI name VCDiploIcon::__CButtonObserverGlue (vftable 0x015CB888) is the glue the constructor writes at +0x24.

struct_fields.name: window
struct_fields.comment: The dialog's window, made by the constructor; the CAsk* constructors look `AgreeButton`, `DeclineButton`, `Title` and `Description` up in it.
struct_fields.evidence: `param_1[1] = window` in the constructor 0x63D4B0 and the lookups through [this+4] slot 13 in every CAsk* constructor.

struct_fields.name: closed
struct_fields.comment: Set by a button that has done its work; slot 1 then answers false and the idler deletes the dialog.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov byte [esi+0x64], 1` in CDiplomacyDialog::Accept/Decline and in the request dialogue's agree/cancel; zeroed by the constructor; read as `(char)this[0x19] == 0` by slot 1.

struct_fields.name: host
struct_fields.comment: The in-game screen the dialog was made for; Accept and Decline post their command through its slot 18.
struct_fields.evidence: Stored from ECX by each CAsk* constructor (`param_1[0x1a] = this`); read as the poster in 0x60FAF8 and 0x60FB38.

struct_fields.name: action
struct_fields.comment: The dialog's own clone of the offer (slot 16 of the pending action); Accept/Decline set its type and post it, the slot 7 tests read its date. The destructor deletes it while it is still valid.
struct_fields.evidence: `param_1[0x1b] = action->slot16()` in each constructor; `mov eax,[esi+0x6c]; mov [eax+0x18], 2` in 0x60FAE3; the destructor 0x6147B0.

struct_fields.name: dialog
struct_fields.comment: The offer's dialog, opened on a click (and then cleared) or declined after seven days.

struct_fields.name: kind
struct_fields.comment: Which kind of offer, 1..13 as the AskPlayer bodies number them (1 peace, 2 alliance, 3 trade, 4 access asked, 5 access offered, 6 call to arms, 7 NAP, 8 faction, 9 expedition, 10 licence, 11 debt, 12 and 13 lend-lease asked and offered). Its reader was not traced.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov [edi+8], ecx` at 0x61974C with ECX the kind from 0x61A212.

struct_fields.name: from
struct_fields.comment: The proposer, whose flag the icon shows.
struct_fields.evidence: Copied from the tag argument at 0x619754-0x61975C.

struct_fields.name: bar
struct_fields.comment: The diplomatic message bar holding it (CInGameIdler +0x1D38).

struct_fields.name: shown_at
struct_fields.evidence: Stamped from g_CCurrentGameState->tick by the constructor.

struct_fields.name: blink_from
struct_fields.comment: shown_at + 120 hours: from here the icon blinks.

struct_fields.name: expires_at
struct_fields.comment: shown_at + 168 hours: past it the offer is declined for the player.

struct_fields.name: clicked
struct_fields.comment: Set by CDiploIcon::OnClick; the next update drops the icon.
struct_fields.evidence: Written at the end of 0x619D80, tested at 0x619C0F.

struct_fields.name: laid_out
struct_fields.comment: Set by DiploIconBar_Layout for an icon it placed; only such an icon blinks.

struct_fields.name: diplo_icon_bar
struct_fields.comment: The diplomatic message bar: the icons of offers waiting for the player. CInGameIdler::AddDiplomaticOffer adds to it; UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows runs DiploIconBar_Update on it each frame.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov edi, [edi+0x1d38]` before the call to 0x61A1D0 at 0x674F98; the UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows record's call through 0x219E80.

struct_fields.name: pending_diplomatic_actions_no_unlink
struct_fields.comment: The fourth member of the pending list's CList (head +0xF24, tail +0xF28, count +0xF2C): while set, a removal marks the node's +0xC byte instead of unlinking it.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp byte [ebx+0xf30], 0; je <unlink>; mov byte [eax+0xc], 1` at 0x4DB101-0x4DB10A, the CList::no_unlink shape at +0xC of a list starting at +0xF24.

struct_fields.name: next_offer_allowed
struct_fields.revises: comment only: the field has a reader now (CCountry::HasDiplomatEnroute), so 'no reader was found' is withdrawn. Name and type kept.
struct_fields.comment:
A tick (hours), set to the proposal's `date + 0xA8` - **exactly seven days** - by CDiplomacyStatus::SetNextOfferAllowed (0xA4A550), whose one caller is CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute on the PROPOSE path, for every kind of action except `callaction` (0x309), on the proposer's status toward the recipient. **Read by CCountry::HasDiplomatEnroute (rva 0xE3ED0), `tick <= this`**: while it holds the proposer has "a diplomat enroute" to that country - the diplomacy screen greys the row and shows ENROUTE with this date, and the AI scripts skip that country. Execute does not test it, so an offer posted regardless (Lua's PostAction with no check) is not refused. The setter's own comparison against `tick + 0xA8` is dead - both arms store the same value.

**The game's own name for the field is `last_send_diplomat`**: CDiplomacyStatus::LoadKey (rva 0x648190) stores that key, token 0x306, here at 0xA482C1 through Date_SetFromString. The code is on the record's side about tense: what is stored is the date the diplomat arrives, seven days in the future. So the key is noted and the behavioural name kept.
struct_fields.evidence: The reader at 0x4E3F6E and the scan described on SetNextOfferAllowed's entry, with its two positive controls.

slots_noted: CEU3Idler::Update (rva 0x244750) is revised here for its comment only; its slot, CEU3Idler slot 1, is already recorded as Update and is not repeated. Every other slot a function of this fragment sits in is recorded above.
